analysis: The PR only changes documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md adds a 'Calibration ownership and foreground admission' section (head lines 335-362) and a code-map row (line 412), and docs/architecture/inference.md adds 'Model startup calibration' plus code-map rows. No code, keys, wire fields, or coordinator contracts change, and the docs state that capacity wire fields and the platform memory contract are unchanged. The documented behavior is local to the provider. Startup health and calibration probes are synthetic: a local-only EngineMeasurementPurpose.startupWarmup, an excluded warmup, and 'uncached solo probes'. They carry no consumer data, so A-001 exposure does not grow. Because the probes are described as uncached, they should not add SSD prefix-cache donations, so the T-041 at-rest surface and its SEC-035 sign-off appear unaffected. Memory floors, activation and OS reserves, and concurrency ceilings are stated as unchanged. A customer request cancels calibration and waits for actual retirement before admission, which keeps customer service available (T-010, T-029 not weakened). Original first-content deadlines still apply. Calibration publishes measured rates through existing capacity heartbeats. Those are provider-self-reported and so adversarial (ADV-001), but that was already true and is not new here. The next pass should check the code behind the docs (IdleCalibrationCoordinator, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration*, EnginePerformanceMeasurements). It should confirm that probe prompts never reach the prefix-cache donate path and that foreground cancellation cannot hold request memory reservations. This unit set contained no source code, so those points are unverified.
